Step 2: Atmospheric Multi-Gas Evolution & Climate Treaties (1979–2026)
Synthetic Base Index

Atmospheric greenhouse gases normalized to Base = 100, plotted alongside the 12-month rolling mean surface temperature anomaly and international environmental treaty milestones.

  • Carbon Dioxide (CO₂): Climbed by +27.3% (336 to 428 ppm), serving as the relentless baseline accumulator of radiative forcing.
  • Methane (CH₄): Rose by +18.8% (1,635 to 1,942 ppb), with rapid acceleration resuming after 2007.
  • Nitrous Oxide (N₂O): Rose by +7.6% (316 to 340 ppb) over the post-2001 window.
  • CFC-12 (Montreal Protocol Milestone): Peaked in 2000 at 195% of its 1979 baseline, falling to 169% by 2026 under the worldwide phaseout.
  • 2023–2024 Thermal Spike: El Niño and marine heatwaves combined to propel monthly surface anomalies to a peak of +0.93 °C.

Step 4: Empirical Sensitivity Regressions & CFC Regime Decoupling
Matplotlib Bug Resolved

Resolved the linewidth alias crash and modeled temperature response across all greenhouse gases with 95% confidence intervals.

  • Panel A (CO₂): Sensitivity of +0.0113 °C per ppm ($R^2 = 0.799$). Every 10 ppm increase corresponds to +0.113 °C warming.
  • Panel B (CH₄): Sensitivity of +0.00387 °C per ppb ($R^2 = 0.781$). A 100 ppb methane rise corresponds to +0.387 °C warming.
  • Panel C (N₂O): Sensitivity of +0.02961 °C per ppb ($R^2 = 0.683$), reflecting high per-molecule radiative efficiency.
  • Panel D (CFC-12): Highlights the historical decoupling. From 1979–1995, CFC-12 correlated positively ($r = +0.257$). After 2001, global phaseout inverted the correlation to $r = −0.834$.
🌪️
Step 5: Weather Noise vs. Climate Signal — Monthly vs. Annual Regressions
Noise Cancellation

Monthly observations contain high-frequency weather noise (ENSO, regional storms, volcanic aerosols; σ ≈ 0.18 °C). Aggregating into 12-month annual averages filters out stochastic fluctuations:

  • Correlation Leap: On an annual climatological basis, CO₂ correlation leaps from r = +0.8941 to r = +0.9390.
  • Explained Variance: $R^2$ expands from 79.9% to 88.2%.
  • Slope Invariance: The regression slope remains identical (+0.0113 °C/ppm), confirming weather noise does not bias the physical warming rate.

Step 7: Planetary Metabolism — Dual Seasonality of CO₂ and CH₄
Biogeochemical Sinks

Atmospheric concentrations exhibit rhythmic seasonal deviations that reveal Earth's natural metabolic processes:

  • CO₂ Biosphere Seasonality: Driven by Northern Hemisphere vegetation. Summer photosynthesis draws down carbon (trough in September at −2.64 ppm), while winter plant decay and respiration release it (April peak at +1.75 ppm).
  • CH₄ Photochemical Sink: Governed by atmospheric chemistry. Summer sunlight produces abundant hydroxyl radicals (OH) that destroy methane, producing a distinct July trough (−8.77 ppb).
